QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_14

question.text: Secondary data for a Social Impact Assessment includes:

answer.text: Primary survey results collected specifically for the current SIA
FGD transcripts created during the current engagement
Records routinely maintained by the organisation, data in the public domain, monthly/quarterly/six-monthly reports, case studies, photo documentation; RTI data where relevant
Only audited financial statements of the SE

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 5.8 explains secondary data as 'readily available through a repository of information available with the organisation. The records that are maintained by the organisation as a part of their routine project activity are an example of secondary data. Data available in the public domain is also secondary data... If need be, Social Impact Assessors can obtain data from any public authority under RTI.' Includes photo documentation, film clippings, case study reports, intake sheets. The Trap: Primary survey (A) and FGD transcripts (B) are PRIMARY data — collected first-hand for the assignment. Audited financials (D) are only one sub-type of secondary data, not the full set. Cross-Exam Context: NISM XV (RA) uses 'primary vs secondary' in a markets-research context. XXIII's nuance is the RTI channel — uniquely available to SIAs for government-scheme data. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Before fieldwork, file an RTI request for beneficiary lists, fund-flow statements, and MIS data of any co-funding government scheme — this arms you with an independent counterfactual baseline for attribution testing.
